# ADR-0017: Measure task DAGs — the engine walks the ladder

> **Status:** proposed | **Date:** 2026-07-18

**References:** [ADR-0001](../adr/ADR-0001.md), [ADR-0005](../adr/ADR-0005.md), [ADR-0013](../adr/ADR-0013.md), [ADR-0016](../adr/ADR-0016.md), [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md)

## Context

GPU-measured code domains grade through a sequence of oracles (CPU self-check, single-GPU diff, ncu capture, multi-GPU equality, compute-sanitizer). The sequence lives inside an opaque 800-line domain gate script. Three incidents exposed the cost: no per-step resume (run 13 repaid all proven steps after a pod restart), silent 8-hour Kubernetes retries on transient failures, and generic judge policy reimplemented independently per domain.

## Decision

The manifest declares the measurement DAG as data ([[measure.task]]), and the engine walks it. Named job templates replace the fixed benchmark/lm_eval/profile trio. Tasks are connected by depends_on edges with a typed validity model (required vs advisory, substrate capabilities, hardware truncation computed before dispatch). TaskDagJudge sits behind the existing Judge trait. The walker is a ready-set loop; v1 pins max_inflight=1. Retry policy splits on classification: measured failure is never retried, transport failures get bounded auto-retry. Cache keys derive from session log fold. Amendment: a task's $OUT may carry explicit status (including skipped).

## Consequences

Generic judge policy written once in Rust. The next codegen domain declares ~40 TOML lines instead of copying the 800-line walker. Per-task cache keys make regrade incremental. Single-shot domains keep measure_cmd unchanged. Cost: the DAG walker adds engine complexity and the typed validity model introduces new failure modes (hardware truncation, substrate mismatch).

## Alternatives Considered

### Engine-owned DAG walker with typed task validity model (accepted)


### Broker-side orchestration: let the broker walk the measurement sequence (rejected)

- **Rejected because:** Recreates the opaque single-call problem; the broker becomes the new 800-line script.

### Gate script as thin grader: keep opaque script but thin it to a grading wrapper (rejected)

- **Rejected because:** Preserves the copy-paste channel between domains; thin wrapper still duplicates judge policy.

### Generic engine DAG framework: full-featured DAG execution engine (rejected)

- **Rejected because:** Scope creep; the measurement ladder is specific enough that a narrow walker outperforms a generic framework.
